paper.title: Dynamics of working memory drift and information flow across the cortical hierarchy
paper.abstract: Working memory representations are not static but undergo systematic drift during retention. Using 7T fMRI with layer-specific imaging, we tracked information flow across V1, V3AB, and IPS during a delayed-estimation task. Memory drift originated in deep layers of V3AB and propagated to superficial V1 layers via feedback connections. Drift magnitude predicted estimation bias on a trial-by-trial basis, consistent with drift-diffusion dynamics. Population responses maintained orientation tuning geometry but shifted along orthogonal dimensions, suggesting memory encoding in a subspace distinct from sensory coding.

paper.title: Serial dependence operates on categorical rather than physical representations
paper.abstract: We demonstrate that serial dependence in orientation estimation arises from categorical representations, not continuous physical features. Using a morph-space task (N=42), participants showed attractive bias toward previous trial's category boundary, not its physical value. A hierarchical Bayesian model with categorical priors explained the pattern better than continuous updating models (BIC difference = 47.3). These results suggest serial dependence reflects high-level categorical inference rather than low-level sensory adaptation.

paper.title: Voxel-wise pRF mapping reveals layer-dependent radial bias in human V1-V4
paper.abstract: We developed a novel layer-specific pRF mapping technique using 7T fMRI that independently estimates radial and tangential components of receptive field elongation across cortical depth. In V1, deep layers showed stronger radial bias (ratio = 1.42 ± 0.08) while superficial layers were more isotropic (ratio = 1.12 ± 0.06). This gradient reversed in V4, where superficial layers exhibited the strongest co-axial organization. The method resolves degeneracy in standard pRF models by fitting oriented gratings at multiple reference angles.
